name: pulls_open_draft
description: Open one draft pull request on Ledgerline's repository, proposing in prose the change to the file a triage names. It is a draft: it merges nothing, needs no commits, and can be closed. Open it before the triage comment, and never for an issue whose file is none. The branch must be exactly repomind/issue-<number>. Returns JSON {pr, issue, branch, status}: pr is its identifier, such as pr-3; status is opened, or already_open when this run already has an open pull request from that branch, in which case nothing new was opened (a retry is safe: the harness keys every write). The title is at most 120 characters and the body at most 4,000; an empty title or body is an error and opens nothing.

number.description: The number of the issue the pull request addresses: 4192 for issue-4192.

branch.description: Exactly repomind/issue-<number>, such as repomind/issue-4192. Any other branch is an error: one branch per issue is how a repeated request finds the pull request it already opened.

title.description: One line, at most 120 characters, saying what the change fixes or adds, such as: Cap the retry delay at maxDelayMs.

body.description: At most 4,000 characters of prose: the file to change, exactly as the triage names it, what is wrong there, and the change you propose. No code is needed.

input.title: Cap the retry delay at maxDelayMs
input.body:
File: src/util/retry.ts

backoffDelay doubles the delay on every attempt and never applies maxDelayMs. Proposed change: return the smaller of the doubled delay and maxDelayMs.

examples.note: Typical: the branch from the issue number, a one-line title, and a body that names the file and proposes the change.

input.title: Document the page size limit in the API guide
input.body:
File: docs/API.md

The guide never says that page sizes above 100 are clamped. Proposed change: add one sentence under Pagination.

examples.note: Hard: a docs triage still opens a pull request, against the document. Only a question, whose file is none, opens none.
